## Up front: what I could and could not do here

I have **no structure-prediction, docking, or protein-design tools available in this session** — no RFdiffusion/RFantibody, no ProteinMPNN, no AlphaFold/Boltz, no PDB fetch, no shell. So I did not compute anything. Everything below is from my own knowledge of HEWL, of the published anti-lysozyme VHH structures, and of standard nanobody-engineering practice. There are no pLDDT, ipTM, ΔΔG or Kd numbers reported below for the new design, because I could not generate any — any number I gave you would be invented.

What I can give you is a complete, specific, executable design: target/epitope definition with residue numbers, a concrete VHH construct sequence with per-residue rationale, and the exact validation pipeline to run.

---

## 1. Target characterisation (PDB 1DPX)

1DPX is hen egg-white lysozyme (HEWL), a single 129-residue chain, solved in the triclinic form at ~1.65 Å (Weiss, Palm & Hilgenfeld, *Acta Cryst D* 2000; crystallised at pH 8.0 with MPD). Single polypeptide, chain A, four disulfides: **Cys6–Cys127, Cys30–Cys115, Cys64–Cys80, Cys76–Cys94**.

Mature sequence (UniProt P00698, residues 19–147 of the precursor = 1–129 mature):

```
  1 KVFGRCELAA AMKRHGLDNY RGYSLGNWVC AAKFESNFNT QATNRNTDGS
 51 TDYGILQINS RWWCNDGRTP GSRNLCNIPC SALLSSDITA SVNCAKKIVS
101 DGNGMNAWVA WRNRCKGTDV QAWIRGCRL
```

Properties that matter for design: very rigid (4 S–S bonds, Tm ≈ 72–75 °C), basic (pI ≈ 11.3) — so the paratope should be **net acidic** for electrostatic steering, and SPR/ITC buffers must have enough salt to avoid nonspecific sticking.

## 2. Epitope selection: the substrate-binding cleft

**Chosen epitope — the glycosidase active-site cleft (subsites A–F)**, centred on the catalytic pair and its aromatic walls:

| HEWL residue (1DPX numbering) | Role in the paratope interface |
|---|---|
| **Glu35** | Catalytic acid; H-bond acceptor/donor at cleft apex |
| **Asp52** | Catalytic nucleophile/stabiliser; salt-bridge target |
| Gln57, Asn59 | Subsite C H-bond network |
| **Trp62, Trp63** | Aromatic platform — stacking target |
| Asp101 | Cleft rim, salt-bridge target |
| Ala107, **Trp108**, Val109 | Hydrophobic cleft wall |

Rationale: (i) **precedent** — the camelid VHH **cAb-Lys3** binds exactly here, with a long CDR3 that inserts into the cleft and acts as a substrate mimic and competitive inhibitor; its complex with HEWL is **PDB 1MEL** (Desmyter *et al.*, *Nat Struct Biol* 1996). Reported affinity is in the nanomolar range (from recollection of that literature — verify against the primary paper before quoting). (ii) **Shape complementarity** — a concave cleft is the natural match for the protruding convex CDR3 that single-domain antibodies, unlike conventional Fvs, can deliver. (iii) **Function** — binding here gives you an inhibitor, so you get a cheap functional readout (enzyme assay) in addition to a binding readout.

## 3. Two routes — recommendation

**Route A (recommended first, highest success probability): precedent-guided CDR grafting.** Take the cAb-Lys3 CDR1/CDR2/CDR3 from **PDB 1MEL** (the VHH chain SEQRES) and graft onto a humanised universal VHH scaffold (h-NbBcII10FGLA, Vincke *et al.*, *JBC* 2009, 284:3273), then affinity-mature CDR3 by site-saturation at the cleft-contacting apex. I am deliberately **not** writing out the cAb-Lys3 sequence — I don't trust my recall of 24 specific residues, and a wrong one would silently poison the whole construct. Pull it from the PDB entry.

**Route B (de novo, what I've drafted below): epitope-directed design on a humanised VHH scaffold.** Lower prior probability of success per candidate, but it is the honest answer to "design a nanobody," and it is what RFantibody would be seeded with.

## 4. Proposed construct — NbLys-D1 (de novo draft)

126 aa, humanised VH3-type VHH framework, FR2 camelid hallmarks retained, engineered CDR1–CDR3 interloop disulfide:

```
QVQLVESGGGLVQPGGSLRLSCAAS GRTFSSYCMG WFRQAPGKEREFVA AISWSGGSTR
YADSVKGRFTISRDNAKNTVYLQMNSLKPEDTAVYYCAA CRGWSYAARTYWSPLDY WGQGTQVTVSS
```

Single-line:
`QVQLVESGGGLVQPGGSLRLSCAASGRTFSSYCMGWFRQAPGKEREFVAAISWSGGSTRYADSVKGRFTISRDNAKNTVYLQMNSLKPEDTAVYYCAACRGWSYAARTYWSPLDYWGQGTQVTVSS`

| Segment | Residues (linear) | Sequence | Design intent |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR1 | 1–25 | QVQLVESGGGLVQPGGSLRLSCAAS | VH3 framework; **Cys22** of canonical S–S |
| CDR1 | 26–35 | GRTFSSY**C**MG | **Cys33** for interloop disulfide |
| FR2 | 36–49 | WFRQAPGKEREFVA | Camelid hallmarks Phe37/Glu44/Arg45/Phe47 — the hydrophilic former-VL face that makes VHHs soluble as single domains |
| CDR2 | 50–59 | AISWSGGST**R** | Terminal Arg to reach the Asp101 cleft rim |
| FR3 | 60–98 | YADSVKGRFTISRDNAKNTVYLQMNSLKPEDTAVYYCAA | **Cys95** of canonical S–S |
| **CDR3** | 99–115 | **CRGWSYAARTYWSPLDY** | 17-residue protruding cleft-inserting loop (below) |
| FR4 | 116–126 | WGQGTQVTVSS | — |

CDR3 per-residue intent, reading into the cleft: **C99** pairs with Cys33 to rigidify the long loop (the camelid solution to CDR3 entropy); **R100** → salt bridge to HEWL Asp101; **G101** stem hinge; **W102** → stacks on the Trp62/Trp63 platform; **S103–Y104** → Tyr hydroxyl H-bonds the Glu35 carboxylate; **A105–A106** → small apex that slots into subsites C/D, the substrate-mimicry element copied in principle from cAb-Lys3's Ala insertion; **R107** → ion pair with catalytic Asp52; **T108** → H-bond Asn59; **Y109–W110** → aromatic clamp against the Ala107/Trp108/Val109 wall; **S111-P112-L113** rigid descending segment (Pro to restrict loop entropy); **D114-Y115** canonical pre-FR4 stem.

Disulfides: Cys22–Cys95 (canonical) + **Cys33–Cys99** (engineered interloop). No unpaired cysteines.

Developability pre-screen I did by inspection of the sequence: **no NG or NS deamidation motifs and no DG/DS isomerisation motifs in any CDR**; **no N-X-S/T glycosylation sequon** anywhere (the framework's N76-T77-V78 and N83-S84-L85 are not sequons); no Met in a CDR; CDR net charge is slightly basic (2 Arg) — which is a flag worth revisiting, because HEWL is strongly basic (pI ~11.3), so if Route B designs fail, inverting CDR2/CDR3 charge toward acidic is the first thing I'd try.

Expression construct: pMES4 or pHEN6c, PelB or DsbA signal peptide for periplasmic export, C-terminal Myc-His6, *E. coli* WK6; or pET22b + SHuffle.

## 5. Validation pipeline (what to actually run — I could not run any of this)

**Structure prep.** 1DPX chain A only; strip waters, MPD, ions; protonate at pH 7.4; keep all four disulfides.

**In silico, in order:**
1. **RFantibody** (RFdiffusion fine-tuned for antibody/VHH, Bennett *et al.*) — specify hotspots `A35, A59, A62, A63, A101, A107`, VHH framework, CDR3 length 16–20. Generate 10³–10⁴ backbones; this replaces my hand-drawn CDR3 with sampled ones.
2. **ProteinMPNN** sequence design on the CDR loops only, framework fixed, 8 sequences per backbone.
3. **Refolding filter** — AlphaFold3 / Boltz-2 / RF2 on the VHH–HEWL complex. Keep designs with interface PAE < 10 Å, ipTM > 0.8, and CDR3 RMSD to the design model < 2 Å. Note that AF2/AF3 are well documented to be unreliable on antibody–antigen interfaces, so treat this as a coarse filter, not a ranking.
4. **Rosetta InterfaceAnalyzer / FoldX ΔΔG** and **PRODIGY** for binding-energy estimates; **3 × 200 ns MD** (OpenMM or GROMACS) on the top ~20, scoring contact persistence of the Glu35/Asp52/Trp62-63 contacts.
5. Order **50–200** designs, not one. Published de novo binder campaigns, nanobodies included, have per-design hit rates of a few percent at best.

**Wet lab:** periplasmic expression in WK6 → Ni-NTA + SEC → (a) **SPR/BLI** against biotinylated HEWL for Kd/kon/koff; (b) **competitive-inhibition assay** — *Micrococcus luteus* (*lysodeikticus*) cell-wall turbidity loss at 450 nm, or EnzChek fluorescein-labelled substrate; a cleft binder must inhibit, which is a far stronger specificity test than binding alone; (c) nanoDSF Tm (expect 60–70 °C for a good VHH); (d) SEC-MALS for monomericity; (e) cross-reactivity panel vs. turkey/human lysozyme to map specificity. Positive control throughout: cAb-Lys3 (1MEL).

**Fallback if Route B yields nothing:** synthetic VHH library (e.g. a long-CDR3 nanobody library) displayed on yeast or phage, selected against biotinylated HEWL with soluble free HEWL competition — the empirical route, and the one that produced cAb-Lys3 in the first place.

## 6. Confidence

- Target facts and epitope residue numbers: **high** — HEWL is one of the best-characterised proteins and 1MEL establishes the cleft as a real, druggable VHH epitope.
- The specific NbLys-D1 sequence binding HEWL with useful affinity as written: **low**. It is a rationally constructed hypothesis, not a validated or computationally scored design. It is a reasonable thing to put into the pipeline above, not a thing to order and expect to work.
- cAb-Lys3 affinity "low nanomolar": **medium** recollection — check the primary paper.

## ANSWER

**Epitope (PDB 1DPX, chain A):** the catalytic cleft — Glu35, Asp52, Gln57, Asn59, Trp62, Trp63, Asp101, Ala107, Trp108, Val109. Precedent: anti-HEWL VHH cAb-Lys3 binds this cleft as a competitive inhibitor (**PDB 1MEL**).

**Proposed nanobody NbLys-D1** (126 aa, humanised VHH scaffold, CDR3 = CRGWSYAARTYWSPLDY, engineered Cys33–Cys99 interloop disulfide plus canonical Cys22–Cys95):

```
QVQLVESGGGLVQPGGSLRLSCAASGRTFSSYCMGWFRQAPGKEREFVAAISWSGGSTR
YADSVKGRFTISRDNAKNTVYLQMNSLKPEDTAVYYCAACRGWSYAARTYWSPLDYWGQGTQVTVSS
```

**Recommended first route is not this de novo draft but CDR grafting from cAb-Lys3 (take its CDRs from 1MEL SEQRES onto the h-NbBcII10FGLA scaffold), then CDR3 affinity maturation.**

**UNABLE (partial):** no affinity, pLDDT/ipTM, or ΔΔG values are reported because no design or structure-prediction tool was available in this session. NbLys-D1 is a knowledge-based hypothesis that has not been computationally scored or experimentally tested; it must go through the RFantibody → ProteinMPNN → AF3/Boltz → MD filter and wet-lab validation described above, in a batch of 50–200 candidates.
